answer: Rhythm-lock admission uses inter-arrival jitter as a gate: an identity's first actions must arrive with human-scale gaps, and bursts above the rolling median trigger a delay. Crossing that ledge costs the attacker real wall-clock time per identity, since parallel registration collapses into queueing. Each fake identity also needs a distinct timing history to clear the summit of sustained low jitter, so farms pay compute and calendar time rather than fees. The fable that volume alone signals demand fails here, because only traffic shape earns admission.
